name: Power converter
seoTitle: Power converter Calculator — Formula, Units & Example
seoDesc: Power converter: work out power in watts from the power in kilowatts. A free conversion calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Power converter takes the numbers you enter and reports power in watts immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer. It is built for a recipe, a shopping list, a travel plan or a form that asks for a unit you do not use. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Power converter calculator work?
sections.html:
The Power converter takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports power in watts in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the power in kilowatts.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html: • A measured quantity, entered by default in kilowatts. The unit chip switches it to any of the 21 supported units.

sections.title: The formula behind the Power converter calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Power in watts=power in milliwatts
Power in milliwatts=power in kilowatts
Power in milliwatts=power in mechanical horsepowers
Power in milliwatts=power in metric horsepowers
Power in milliwatts=power in BTU per hour
Power in milliwatts=power in kcal per hour

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Power, opening in milliwatts
  • Power, opening in watts
  • Power, opening in kilowatts
  • Power, opening in mechanical horsepowers
  • Power, opening in metric horsepowers
  • Power, opening in British thermal units per hour
  • Power, opening in kilocalories per hour
  • Power, opening in ergs per second

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Power converter earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking a product listing against the measurements you work with
  • Reading a recipe written in units you do not use
  • Filling in a form that asks for imperial or metric values
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the power in kilowatts — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Power converter calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns power in watts, derived from the power in kilowatts. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Power converter calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the power in kilowatts, which is 1 field in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter power in milliwatts in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Power in milliwatts opens in milliwatts and the chip beside it offers 21 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Power converter calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
